author: Katey Psencik
title: Pflugerville resident wins $1 million on scratch-off ticket sold in Austin - NewsBreak
text:
By Katey Psencik ,
12 hours ago Trent Taylor holds in his hand $300 worth of scratch-off lottery tickets that he purchased at a gas station in Kenedy Texas on Friday, April 9, 2021. Taylor says that he dreamed about buying scratch-off lottery tickets while in prison and that he couldn't wait to purchase as much as he could. He says that if he doesn't win at least he supported the Texas public school system. Taylor was released from the John B. Connally Unit prison in Kenedy Texas on Friday, April 9, 2021. Taylor was serving an 11-year sentence for an injury to an elderly person and aggravated robbery. (Ricardo B. Brazziell / American-Statesman) A Pflugerville resident is $1 million richer after winning big on a scratch-off ticket sold in Northeast Austin.
According to the Texas Lottery , the winner — who chose to remain anonymous — bought the $50 Ultimate Millions scratch ticket at Weirdo, located at 13414 Harrisglenn Drive near the intersection of Howard Lane and Dessau Road.
Two of the four top prizes in the game have been claimed, according to the Lottery, which means two other $1 million-winning tickets are still available.
The Lottery said the odds of winning any prize in the game are 1 in 3.59, with prizes starting at $75.
